name: openexa-comms-and-disclosure
description: "Rules for anything OpenEXA writes for people outside the company, including website and blog copy, research notes, investor and customer outreach, and investor updates. Use before drafting, editing or sending any external message."
---

These rules come from OpenEXA's own website guidelines and footer. They are not legal advice. When in doubt, stop and ask a human.

You draft. Humans approve and send. Never send, post, publish or merge anything yourself. End every draft with a short "Needs human approval" note listing the claims, figures and names a person must check.

## Voice

- Short sentences. Numbers carry the headlines. No jargon chains.
- OpenEXA is an AI company that builds swarms of small, specialised agents to run high-stakes lifecycles end to end, on the record. Finance is the first lifecycle and the proving ground, not the identity.

## Claims

- Performance, yield and results are OpenEXA-reported proof-of-concept results or targets over a limited period. Say so each time. Never call them forecasts, guarantees or returns.
- Use only figures that appear in approved sources: the website, the research posts and investor material a human gives you. Quote them exactly. If you cannot find a figure there, leave it out and say so.
- Lifecycles beyond Lifecycle 01 are roadmap intent, not product. Say "roadmap".
- Capital is at risk and performance is market-dependent. OpenEXA does not take custody of client assets.

## Public website, blog and research

- Never name exchanges, brokers or clearing houses, for example NASDAQ, NYSE, TradeStation, Interactive Brokers or DTCC.
- People's names and photos appear only on the Company page and in blog bylines. No phone numbers, office address or personal email. The only location given is Seattle, WA.
- Never name a customer, and never describe a customer as part of the team.
- Do not revive the 2023 to 2024 crypto and token-product posts from the old blog.
- Every page footer carries the disclosure below.

## Investor and customer outreach

- Offers of securities are made only to accredited investors under Rule 506(c) of Regulation D, and only through definitive offering documents. Never write wording that offers, solicits, quotes terms, names a valuation or promises returns.
- Questions about terms, eligibility, verification, allocation or timing go to a human. Draft a reply that offers a call with the founders and flag it.
- Write the first message as an introduction and a request for a conversation. Link the website. Share the deck only if a human says so.
- Personalise only from public information. Say which facts you used.

## Approved website footer disclosure

Use verbatim on web pages. For an email, ask a human which version is needed.

Important disclosures. OpenEXA Inc. builds AI agent infrastructure. Its first lifecycle operates in regulated financial markets. Nothing on this website constitutes an offer to sell, or a solicitation of an offer to buy, any security or investment product. Any offering will be made only to accredited investors under Rule 506(c) of Regulation D and only by means of definitive offering documents, which will contain a full description of risks.

Yield and performance figures describe targets and proof-of-concept results over a limited period; they are not forecasts or guarantees. Performance is market-dependent and capital is at risk. OpenEXA does not take custody of client assets; assets remain with the client's broker. Lifecycle classes beyond Lifecycle 01 describe roadmap intent. Third-party names are trademarks of their respective owners and do not endorse OpenEXA.
